title: Sandpiper Point Rising
premise: Orsen Thornbury, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in scandal a decade ago, has stopped believing in the ceremonies she sells — until her bakery lease runs out and the only buyer for the building is the woman who wrote her anonymous letters from prison: Delia Voss, the sister of the man Orsen's testimony sent away. Delia moves in next door with a decade of unanswered letters and one demand — recant, or lose everything. As they're forced to collaborate on the town's bicentennial wedding festival, Orsen discovers her testimony was coerced by the man she once loved, and must choose between protecting her reputation and telling a truth that could free an innocent man. She forgives herself by testifying again, saving both the bakery and, unexpectedly, falling into a second chance with Delia.
about_author: Sebastian Marchetti is the pen name of a former small-town event coordinator who spent years watching love arrive late, leave early, and occasionally stay. They write romances about people who have to forgive themselves before anyone else can get close.

chapters.title: The Last Cake on the Shelf
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She books another wedding she doesn't believe in while the bakery lease notice sits unopened on her counter. Emotional beat: numb professionalism masking dread.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Opened
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Packing up storage, she finds ten years of unopened letters postmarked from Fairview Correctional, all addressed to her. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a bruise.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia Voss moves into the cottage next door, recognizing Orsen immediately; Orsen doesn't yet know who she is. Emotional beat: coiled patience.

chapters.title: Sandpiper Point at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia walks the beach where her brother was arrested, remembering the night that split two families. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: You Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Delia reveals her identity over the bakery counter, letters spread between them like evidence. Emotional beat: exposure, shame, defiance.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The building's new owner is revealed to be Delia; eviction looms unless Orsen meets her terms. Emotional beat: cornered desperation.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Delia offers a deal: publicly recant her testimony before the bicentennial festival, or lose the bakery. Orsen refuses but can't walk away. Emotional beat: hostile negotiation.

chapters.title: Forced Collaboration
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The town council conscripts both women to co-produce the bicentennial wedding festival. Emotional beat: reluctant proximity, sparks of grudging respect.

chapters.title: What Marcus Told Me to Say
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Flashback chapter: young Orsen coached by her then-fiancé Marcus before the grand jury, his hand on her shoulder. Emotional beat: dawning horror at her own complicity.

chapters.title: Flour and Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Baking together for the festival tasting, the enemies find unexpected rhythm; Delia sees the woman behind the witness. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through armor.

chapters.title: The Festival Gains a Groom
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Marcus returns to town as the festival's headline sponsor, charming and threatening in equal measure. Emotional beat: old fear reawakened.

chapters.title: A Letter Finally Answered
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia reads Orsen's first written reply — not a recantation, but a question about her brother's alibi. Emotional beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: Threats in Wedding White
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Marcus warns Orsen privately that reopening the case destroys them both; he reminds her what he protected her from. Emotional beat: terror versus clarity.

chapters.title: The Alibi Nobody Checked
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Digging through festival archives, the women find a dock logbook proving Danny Voss was miles away during the robbery. Emotional beat: shared mission ignites real intimacy.

chapters.title: Kiss at the Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. After a festival disaster bonds them, Orsen and Delia kiss — then Orsen pulls away, still unable to face what testifying means. Emotional beat: longing colliding with self-loathing.

chapters.title: What I Was Afraid Of
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia confronts why she really came: not vengeance, but needing someone to say her brother's name without flinching. Emotional beat: vulnerability offered and withheld.

chapters.title: The Man in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen finally reads every letter, weeping through a decade of Danny's innocence and her own cowardice. Emotional beat: reckoning with the person in the mirror.

chapters.title: Blackmail at the Altar
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marcus threatens to expose Orsen's forged signature on the original lease unless she stays silent; Delia discovers the threat. Emotional beat: betrayal, protectiveness, resolve.

chapters.title: Testimony, Second Reading
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Climax: at the festival's closing ceremony, before the whole town, Orsen publicly recants, naming Marcus as the man who coerced her. Emotional beat: liberation at maximum cost.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Fallout: Orsen loses clients and standing; Marcus flees under investigation; Danny's exoneration petition moves forward. Emotional beat: ruin that feels like relief.

chapters.title: Bread for Two
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Delia tears up the eviction, offering partnership instead; Orsen, forgiven by the mirror if not yet by the town, chooses to stay and rebuild. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.

chapters.title: Sandpiper Point Rising
chapters.summary: Dual POV. One year later: Danny comes home, the bakery thrives, and Orsen plans one last wedding — her own, small and true, on the beach at low tide. Emotional beat: second chances, finally well-timed.
